identity.title: The kinematics of massive high-redshift dusty star-forming galaxies
identity.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

paper_type_evidence.quote: We demonstrate our method on ALMA observations of $^{12}$CO (2$-$1), (3$-$2) or (4$-$3) emission lines from an initial sample of 30 massive 850$\mu$m-selected dusty star-forming galaxies

targets.name: ALESS DSFGs (30 sources in ECDFS, e.g. ALESS 122.1, 073.1)

evidence.quote: We focus on the analysis of ALMA observations of sources located in the ECDFS field from that study, which are part of the ALESS survey

question.value: Can galaxy kinematics be modelled directly in visibility space for massive high-z DSFGs, and what do the results imply for alpha_CO, the Tully-Fisher relation and links to local early-type galaxies?

evidence.quote: performing the optimization of the kinematic model parameters directly in visibility-space instead of the conventional approach of fitting velocity fields produced with the clean algorithm in real-space

analysis_steps.goal: Select sample by integrated SNR and classify

method.value: Integrated SNR >8 cut; velocity maps from single-Gaussian fits per pixel of dirty cubes; visual classes

evidence.quote: we found that the parameters of our model were effectively unconstrained when modelling sources with an integrated SNR $< 8$

analysis_steps.goal: Fit 3D thick rotating disk in uv-plane

method.value: Galpak3D disk models (exponential flux, isothermal velocity profile, h_z=0.15 R_1/2) transformed by pyNUFFT per channel; Gaussian likelihood on visibilities

evidence.quote: our model is comprised of 10 free parameters

key_parameters.value: Gaussian prior on centre (sigma 1 arcsec); uniform Vmax 0-600 km/s, sigma 0-200 km/s, r_e 0-2", r_t 0-1"

fitting.value: Nested sampling with PyMultinest; median of marginalised posteriors, 68% intervals

evidence.quote: we use a nested sampling Monte Carlo technique of Skilling (2006) implemented in the PyMultinest algorithm

validation.value: Simulated observations recover true parameters within 3 sigma; comparison with ALESS 122.1 and 073.1 literature

evidence.quote: In general we find that we always recover the true input parameters within 3$\sigma$.

analysis_steps.goal: Derive circularized velocity and dynamical mass

method.value: V_circ corrected for asymmetric drift at 2 r_e; M_dyn = r V_circ^2/G within 10 kpc

evidence.quote: the circularized velocity computed at a twice the effective radius and the dynamical mass computed within a radius of $r=$ 10 kpc
Assuming a constant velocity dispersion profile and considering that the vertical profile of our thick disk model does not depend on the radius

method.value: Equate M_dyn to gas + stellar + dark matter mass; per-source values with bootstrapped errors, combined into joint constraint

evidence.quote: We compute the value of $\alpha_{\rm CO}$ and its associated error (via bootstrapping) for each of the sources in our sample.

evidence.quote: we assume a fixed dark matter fraction, $f_{\rm dm} = 0.25$

method.value: Orthogonal distance regression with slope fixed to local value, fitting offset b

findings_qualitative.value: DSFGs lie on the high-mass end of the Tully-Fisher relations of typical star-forming galaxies.

evidence.quote: Our DSFGs occupy the high-mass end of these relations, but have normalisations that are consistent with those measured for the KMOS$^{\rm 3D}$ sources.

claims.hypothesis: Massive DSFGs prefer a starburst-like alpha_CO
claims.experiment: Dynamical mass minus stellar and dark matter mass divided by L_CO(1-0)

evidence.quote: Our approach yields an estimate of $\alpha_{\rm CO} = 0.92 \pm 0.36$

claims.hypothesis: Disk-like DSFGs follow the TFR of typical SFGs
claims.experiment: ODR fit with fixed local slopes
claims.finding: They extend the TFR to higher masses

evidence.quote: Hence, the key conclusion from this comparison is the massive nature of these disk-like DSFGs, that appear to just extend the scaling relations found in less massive galaxies.

claims.hypothesis: DSFGs are progenitors of local massive early-type galaxies
claims.experiment: Mb–sigma plane comparison and space densities
claims.result: Median within ~1σ of z~0 trend; density 4–5e-5 Mpc^-3

evidence.quote: This provides further support for the existence of an evolutionary link

why_this_method.value: uv-plane fitting gives well-defined Gaussian errors and avoids clean-dependent preprocessing

evidence.quote: because the errors on the visibilities are well defined (i.e., Gaussian errors)

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Gaussian flux and Freeman velocity profiles tried for complex sources; same unphysical behaviour

evidence.quote: we also tried different functional forms for both the flux profile (e.g., Gaussian) and the velocity profile (e.g., Freeman model)

limitations_admitted.value: Modest resolution may misclassify mergers as disks

evidence.quote: the modest resolution of our data can lead, in some cases, to a misclassification of mergers as disks

referee_caveats_inferred: Fixed f_dm=0.25 and SED stellar masses drive alpha_CO; the result is degenerate with these
